about: Heat from field to factory (November 2026): the evidence behind /cotton-and-heat/. Occupational guidance is reused from the factory heat batch (research/2026-11/factory-heat), which the page builder also reads. New here: an ILO programme description from Madhya Pradesh, a commissioned rapid assessment of women cotton farmers in Sindh, two surveys of women cotton pickers in Pakistani Punjab, a news report on payment by weight, a controlled-environment experiment on heat and cotton flowering, an ICAR agronomic review, USDA reports on the Pakistan cotton sector and on ginning, two ginning studies (dust and combustibility) and a news report on early picking in Sindh. Programme descriptions are not evaluations; training delivered is not proof of reduced illness; the crop experiment is not a field result. Named individuals in the sources are not named on the page. Better Cotton's Pakistan page and its account of an individual worker could not be read from the build session and are not used.

claims.text: In Madhya Pradesh, an ILO project with the Confederation of Indian Textile Industry trained small and marginal cotton farmers on adapting working hours in extreme heat, oral rehydration solution, safe postures for carrying loads and warning signs needing medical attention; more than 50 farmers joined a field demonstration in Ratlam district on 11 May 2026.
rests_on: adapting working hours during periods of extreme heat
more than 50 small and marginal cotton farmers

claims.text: The workshops highlighted inadequate access to safe drinking water, sanitation, washing areas, resting spaces and safe transport, and that the farmers lack coverage under labour legislation and social protection systems.
rests_on: washing areas, resting spaces and safe transport
lack coverage under labour legislation and social protection systems

claims.text: Women are often engaged in cotton picking and other labour-intensive tasks in intense heat; a participant described women's added work fetching water in summer, when water availability falls and household demand rises.
The absence of organised associations among cotton farmers and farming communities limits collective dialogue on workplace safety and welfare.
With support from the Confederation of Indian Textile Industry, the project set up a drinking water point using earthen pots.
rests_on: drinking water point using earthen pots

claims.text: Small and marginal cotton farmers are frequently exposed to hazardous agrochemicals, biological dust and prolonged physical strain from repetitive bending and heavy lifting.

In a 2025 rapid assessment of 300 women cotton farmers in four districts of Sindh, commissioned by Better Cotton, 93% sowed seed by hand, 77% weeded and 69% picked cotton, while far fewer operated irrigation or sprayed pesticides.
The same assessment found women's waking hours split almost evenly between cotton farming and unpaid domestic and care work, with only 4% left for leisure or learning.

A 2017 report from Pakistan's cotton belt described cotton picked by hand, with women carrying their bundles to be weighed at the end of the day to determine their pay; women made up the bulk of an estimated half a million cotton pickers.
rests_on: carry their bundles of blooms to be weighed
estimated half a million cotton pickers

claims.text: In Vehari district in Pakistani Punjab, 61% of women cotton pickers from Bt-cotton households and 66% from non-Bt households reported one or more pesticide-related health effects during the picking season.

A survey of 600 women cotton pickers in three Punjab districts found lower health costs among pickers trained in precautionary measures under Better Cotton, and that distance from hospital affected health costs.

In a controlled-environment study of 16 upland cotton cultivars, heat during the reproductive stage (36/24 °C day/night against 32/24 °C) cut pollen germination by 71% and seed cotton and lint yield by 19% and 26% on average; cultivars responded differently.
In Indian Punjab the recommended sowing window for cotton runs from April to mid-May; temperatures of 27 to 32 °C support reproductive development, and most of India's cotton is rainfed.
rests_on: cotton planted in our country is rainfed

claims.text: Cotton fibre becomes extremely sensitive to rain during harvest.
rests_on: extremely sensitive to rain during harvest

claims.text: In 2018, cotton planting in Sindh proceeded from mid-March.
Pakistan's integrated cotton and textile sector was reported to include 1,200 ginneries, 523 textile units and 400 cottonseed crushers and oil refiners.
The quality of picking and ginning in Pakistan results in varying bale sizes and high levels of foreign matter.
In May 2025, picking began early in coastal Sindh, attributed to a sudden rise in temperatures, and gins in Punjab bought raw cotton from Sindh for ginning.
During ginning, cotton fibres are separated from the seeds, cleaned of foreign material and pressed into bales of lint; cotton's value is counted as lint plus seed.
rests_on: cotton fibers are separated from the seeds

claims.text: In the United States cotton is mechanically harvested with specialised equipment, and US yarn and fabric exports often go abroad for further processing before finished products return.
rests_on: for further processing before many of the finished products return

claims.text: Loose cotton fibre from ginning can support smouldering combustion if ignited; in laboratory tests, collected gin dust did not behave as a combustible dust, and dust explosions are unknown in the cotton ginning industry.
rests_on: unknown in the cotton ginning industry

claims.text: In a study of 188 workers in 10 cotton-ginning factories, lung function declined with longer exposure to cotton dust, many workers reported chest tightness and cough, and byssinosis symptoms were observed.
